slides.headline: Separate the **instinct** from the idea.
slides.sub: Mark Pincus on Life at the Speed of Play. Zynga, FarmVille, Words With Friends, Hivemind. A Sourcery episode with Molly O'Shea.

slides.text: Your number one job as a founder is to be **right.**
slides.author: Mark Pincus
slides.role: Life at the Speed of Play

slides.sub: Something broken in human experience. SMS taxi was right. The Tribe.net instincts were right.

columns.b: The emotional vein. Something broken in human experience that keeps pulling you back.
One product bet on that instinct. Often a B+. Kill it fast so the A can show up.
The skill that sharpens with reps. Ask is this it? and you already know.

slides.sub: Run them in that order. Give yourself four shots on goal instead of one grind up a hill.

slides.heading: The order that **wins**

steps.label: Proven
steps.sub: find the closest success, same audience, deconstruct every pixel

steps.label: Better
steps.sub: one change the audience would all notice

steps.label: New
steps.sub: the novel hook, expect it to fail, isolate the experiment

slides.sub: Four shots on goal beat one slow march up a single hill.

slides.label: retention beats virality in consumer
slides.sub: 40,000 games launched. Zero held the top 25. People download zero new apps a month. Build for the life stack.

slides.heading: Why **retention** is the only number
paragraphs: Virality buys you a spike. Day 365 measures whether the spike turned into a habit, and habit is the whole game in consumer.
Forty thousand games launched and none of them held a top 25 spot. Most people add zero new apps to their phone in a month.
So build for the life stack. Earn a place people return to without a push notification dragging them back.

slides.heading: Real CEO, **fake CEO**
slides.body: The real job lives in the product. Great product teams. Products users love. Half the calendar spent here. iPhone home screen research as a daily habit. The fake version tours investors, lectures on culture, chases press and Davos, and pushes an agenda detached from the product.
slides.accentSub: of a real CEO calendar sits inside the product itself.

slides.heading: The tech assistant is **vampire blood**
paragraphs: Bezos, Grove, and Gates each had someone shadow them. Proximity transfers judgment faster than any memo can.
Pluck the talent early, let them shadow the CEO, then hand them a mini-CEO project to ship on their own.
Ian Cinnamon: MIT early, built apps, marked low on paper. As an expert witness he sat closest to the data. Plucked early, shadowed the CEO, went on to found Apex.

slides.sub: The talent a system instinctively pushes out is often the talent worth the most. Non-scalable leverage compounds.
